title: Kenyan Tamarind Sauce
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Tamarind Sauce — a smooth, sweet-sour, deeply flavoured sauce made from tamarind paste, brown sugar, ginger, and spices. The essential dipping sauce for bhajia, viazi karai, and samosa — and an extraordinary glaze for grilled meats.
longDesc: Tamarind sauce occupies a unique space in Kenyan condiments — it is sweet, sour, and complex in a way that no other sauce replicates. The tartaric acid of tamarind pairs with brown sugar's caramel notes, ginger's warmth, and cumin's earthiness to create a sauce that elevates everything it touches. In coastal Kenya it is as fundamental as pili pili.
ingredients: 1 tsp cornstarch dissolved in 2 tbsp water — for thickening
steps: Combine tamarind paste, water, brown sugar, ginger, cumin, chilli (if using), and salt in a small saucepan.
Bring to a gentle boil, stirring to dissolve the sugar.
Reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the cornstarch slurry. Stir continuously until the sauce thickens — about 2 minutes.
Taste and adjust balance — more sugar for sweeter, more tamarind paste for tarter.
Strain through a fine sieve for a completely smooth sauce.
chefTips: Brown sugar adds caramel depth that white sugar cannot — do not substitute.
Taste and adjust the sweet-sour balance at the end — this is entirely personal.
The sauce thickens further as it cools — make it slightly thinner than you want the final result.
commonMistakes: Over-sweetening — the tartness should still be prominent.
Under-cooking — the raw tamarind taste should be cooked out.
cookingScience: Tamarind's tartaric acid is the dominant flavouring compound. Unlike citric acid (lemon), tartaric acid has a more lingering sourness. Brown sugar's molasses provides furfural and other caramelised compounds that complement rather than simply counteract the tartness.
sustainabilityTips: Tamarind trees are drought-tolerant perennials — a sustainable flavouring ingredient.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 2 weeks. Freeze for 3 months.
reheating: Warm gently with a splash of water to restore consistency.
healthBenefits: Tamarind is rich in iron and B vitamins.
Acts as a natural digestive aid.
culturalNote: Tamarind sauce is the quintessential dipping sauce of Swahili coastal cooking — the condiment that makes bhajia and viazi karai complete, and one of the oldest flavourings in East African culinary tradition.
